seams_opened.title: Proactive sign-in on an open server can store a token that the menu then can't distinguish from a real gate
seams_opened.impact: On an open server (no LITHRIM_BFF_TOKEN) validateToken hits /v1/meta which 200s for ANY token, so a proactively-entered token validates + stores; the menu then shows 'Signed in' though the server gate is off. Cosmetic — auth still works; cancel is the escape. Not in scope for this cycle.
seams_opened.evidence: bff.js validateToken returns r.ok; /v1/meta is ungated when the server gate is off (UI-LOGIN-1 comment: 'no 401 ever fires').

report: SESSION-MENU-1 landed clean, tests-first. The LeftRail footer '⋯' is now an always-present session menu (proactive Sign in… when no token, Sign out when authed, a muted status line, a click-outside backdrop), folding in the old token-only key button; bff.signIn() reuses the existing 'lithrim:auth-required' gate event; LoginScreen/AuthGate are now cancelable so a proactive sign-in on an open server isn't a dead-end. RED was 9/9 absent-behavior failures; GREEN is 204/205 with the sole failure being the pre-existing foreign app.test.jsx ModeSwitch case (untouched by this cycle). app.jsx was NEVER staged — both commits are scoped pathspec (RED = session_menu.test.jsx only; GREEN = panes.jsx/auth.jsx/bff.js + the 3 mock files). On audit, the monitor should first confirm git show --stat on both SHAs excludes app.jsx, and that auth.test.jsx + the 3 whole-surface suites stayed green.
